title: Collateral Protection Insurance Billing Terms — Monthly Premium on Placed Coverage
content:
**Where premium is billed.** Collateral Protection Insurance premium is billed only on a tracking record whose status is force-placed.

**Billing periods.** Premium is billed monthly in advance. Each billing period starts on the coverage effective date or on a monthly anniversary of the placement date and ends the day before the next anniversary.

**Amount.** The first period, which starts on the coverage effective date, is prorated by actual days: its premium is the plan's monthly premium multiplied by 12, divided by 365, and multiplied by the calendar days of the period counted from its first day through its last day, both included, rounded half-up to the cent. Every later full period is billed at the monthly premium of the record's plan.

**Excluded contract statuses.** No premium is billed for a period that starts while the contract's status is one of the product's excluded contract statuses.

**How a premium is billed.** A premium is billed as added to the contract balance, which capitalises it on the contract, except that while borrower-submitted proof received within the product's proof-review hold period is still unreviewed, the premium is billed as held pending proof review and does not reach the contract.

- If that proof is then rejected, the held premium is billed again, as added to the contract balance, for the same period, and the held charge is released by a held-premium release refund.
- If it is accepted, the held premium is released the same way and is refunded under the product's cancellation and refund rule for any capitalised periods.

**Earning, rounding and interest.** Premium is earned daily by actual days, every prorated premium is rounded half-up to the cent, and capitalised premium accrues contract interest.

## Hypothetical first period

A hypothetical monthly premium of USD 100.00 and a first period of 20 calendar days: USD 100.00 multiplied by 12 is USD 1200.00; divided by 365 it is about USD 3.2877 per day; multiplied by 20 days it is about USD 65.7534, which rounds half-up to a first-period premium of USD 65.75. Each later full period would bill USD 100.00.

## Billing method at a glance

| Situation when the premium is billed | Billing method | Reaches the contract? |
|---|---|---|
| No unreviewed borrower-submitted proof received within the hold period | added to the contract balance | yes |
| Borrower-submitted proof received within the hold period and still unreviewed | held pending proof review | no |
| Held proof later rejected | billed again as added to the contract balance for the same period; held charge released | yes |
| Held proof later accepted | held charge released; capitalised periods refunded under the cancellation and refund rule | no |
